   - **`src/wakil/app/data/common_words.zip`** (was `.txt`, converted): 17KB zip, member `common_words.txt`, decompressed once at import via stdlib `zipfile` (already used elsewhere for `.whisper` parsing). Sibling **`src/wakil/app/data/common_words.SOURCE.md`** documents provenance (hermitdave/FrequencyWords, MIT license, refresh instructions).

   - **`scripts/classify_eval_failures.py`** (new): council-recommended classification tool. Key functions: `_resolve_targets()` (matches combined pytest-ID strings against the real `(skill, scenario_id)` catalog, avoiding fragile hyphen-splitting), `_pass_rate(client, scenario, transcripts, *, label)` — rewritten per user's "#2" request to print each grading result (`[gen 1/5] PASS` / `FAIL:` + item + reason) immediately rather than only in a final summary. `main()` runs 5x generation + 5x frozen-regrade per scenario, buckets into `(a) deterministic`, `(b) generation variance`, `(c) grading variance`, or `PASSING NOW`.

   - **`scripts/diagnose_eval_noise.py`** (new, earlier diagnostic tool, kept for reuse): grading-vs-generation noise diagnostic, sample of 4 scenarios, N=4 repeats each axis.

   - **SKILL.md files edited during eval-triage** (all in `src/wakil/skills/`): `note-conformance/SKILL.md` (direct-override boundary line), `knowledge-research/SKILL.md` + `knowledge-query/SKILL.md` (name-the-CLI-command instructions, knowledge-research→knowledge-research handoff naming), `source-ingestion/SKILL.md` (dead-end guidance pulled from `references/source-types.md`, kb-commit naming), `skill-authoring/SKILL.md` (override/promotion commands pulled from `references/`, genuine-gap-escalation trap clarification), `note-revision/SKILL.md` (notability-deferral to entity-resolution, attached-companion-document guidance from PR #20), `note-routing/SKILL.md` (Step 5/6 reordering so ambiguity-check gates filename generation), `entity-enrichment/SKILL.md` (PR #20: `@file:`-reference confidence-is-about-linking-not-content clarification, added interactively after running the PR #20 eval scenario and finding a failure), `transcript/SKILL.md` (PR #20: prep-doc agenda-resolution guidance).

   - **`docs/adr/0009-*.md`, `0010-*.md`, `0011-*.md`, `0012-*.md`**: four new ADRs, per user's explicit "document significant decisions via the ADR process" instruction.

58	    """What `prepare_landing` resolved, for `land_ingestion` to commit onto.
59	
60	    `local=True` means no git operations at all — the caller should skip
61	    `land_ingestion` entirely (the `--local` escape hatch)."""

65	    local: bool

68	def commit_message(kind: str, description: str) -> str:
69	    if kind not in COMMIT_PREFIXES:
70	        raise GitServiceError(f"unknown commit kind: {kind}")
71	    return f"wakil {kind}: {description}"

74	def ingest_branch_name(root, title: str) -> str:
75	    date = datetime.now(UTC).date().isoformat()
76	    base = f"wakil/ingest/{date}-{slugify(title, max_length=40)}"
77	    name = base
78	    counter = 1
79	    while git.branch_exists(root, name):
80	        name = f"{base}-{counter}"
81	        counter += 1
82	    return name

85	def ensure_clean_for_branch(config: WorkspaceConfig) -> None:
86	    """Refuse to start or resume a wakil branch on top of uncommitted user
87	    changes."""
88	    info = git.inspect_git(config.root_path)
89	    if not info.is_repo:
90	        raise GitServiceError("Workspace is not a git repository; use --local to write locally.")
91	    changed = git.changed_files(config.root_path)
92	    if changed:
93	        listing = "\n".join(f"  {line}" for line in changed[:10])
94	        raise GitServiceError(
95	            f"Working tree has uncommitted changes; commit or stash them first:\n{listing}"
96	        )

99	def commit_change(
100	    config: WorkspaceConfig,
101	    files: list[str],
102	    kind: str,
103	    description: str,
104	) -> CommitOutcome:
105	    """Commit wakil-written files on the current branch with a wakil
106	    convention message (e.g. `wakil chore: normalize person frontmatter`).
107	    Used by `wakil schema migrate --commit` — a plain local commit, not part
108	    of the per-source branch/PR lifecycle below."""
109	    if not files:
110	        raise GitServiceError("Nothing to commit: no files were written.")
111	    message = commit_message(kind, description)
112	    try:
113	        sha = git.stage_and_commit(config.root_path, files, message)
114	    except git.GitError as exc:
115	        raise GitServiceError(str(exc)) from exc
116	    _record_change(config, files, sha, None, None, description, None, kind)
117	    return CommitOutcome(branch=None, commit_sha=sha, message=message)

120	def prepare_landing(
121	    config: WorkspaceConfig,
122	    *,
123	    source_id: int | None,
124	    title: str,
125	    local: bool = False,
126	) -> LandingContext:
127	    """Call before writing any files. Resolves and switches onto the
128	    source's branch (reusing one already recorded on `Source.git_branch` if
129	    it still exists, fetching it if it only exists on origin, or starting
130	    fresh otherwise), leaving the working tree ready for `apply_capture`/
131	    `apply_enrichment` to write into. `local=True` skips all of this — no
132	    git operations, `land_ingestion` should not be called for this context.
133	
134	    `source_id` is None only for a fresh capture, where the `Source` row
135	    doesn't exist yet; pass the known id from `wakil enrich` so an existing
136	    branch/PR can be resumed.
137	    """
138	    if local:
139	        return LandingContext(branch=None, original_branch=None, local=True)
140	    ensure_clean_for_branch(config)
141	    original_branch = git.inspect_git(config.root_path).branch
142	    state = _load_source_git_state(config, source_id) if source_id is not None else None
143	    if state is not None and state.git_branch:
144	        branch = _resume_source_branch(config, state)
145	    else:
146	        # Prefer the source's own recorded title (set at capture time) over
147	        # the caller-supplied one, which for `wakil enrich` is just a
148	        # placeholder until the enrichment proposal exists.
149	        branch_title = (state.title if state is not None else None) or title
150	        branch = _create_fresh_branch(config, branch_title, follow_up=state is not None)
151	    return LandingContext(branch=branch, original_branch=original_branch, local=False)
152

154	def abandon_landing(config: WorkspaceConfig, context: LandingContext) -> None:
155	    """Nothing was written for this landing context (e.g. enrichment
156	    proposed no files) — return to the original branch if we switched away
157	    from it. No-op for a local context."""
158	    if context.local:
159	        return
160	    _return_to_branch(config.root_path, context.original_branch)

163	def land_ingestion(
164	    config: WorkspaceConfig,
165	    context: LandingContext,
166	    *,
167	    source_id: int,
168	    files: list[str],
169	    title: str,
170	    summary: str | None,
171	    ingest_run_id: int | None,
172	    kind: str,
173	    phase: str,
174	) -> CommitOutcome:
175	    """Commit `files` onto `context.branch` and land the source's PR —
176	    creating it as a draft after capture, or flipping it to ready and
177	    posting a summary comment once enrichment lands on an already-open one.
178	
179	    Not for a local context (`context.local` — the caller should skip
180	    calling this entirely and just report the files were written).
181	    """
182	    if context.local:
183	        raise GitServiceError("land_ingestion called with a local (no-git) context")
184	    if not files:
185	        raise GitServiceError("Nothing to commit: no files were written.")
186	    if phase not in PHASES:
187	        raise GitServiceError(f"unknown phase: {phase!r}")
188	
189	    message = commit_message(kind, f"add {title}")
190	    if summary:
191	        message += f"\n\n{summary}"
192	    try:
193	        sha = git.stage_and_commit(config.root_path, files, message)
194	    except git.GitError as exc:
195	        _return_to_branch(config.root_path, context.original_branch)
196	        raise GitServiceError(str(exc)) from exc
197	
198	    _remember_source_branch(config, source_id, context.branch)
199	    try:
200	        pr_url = _land_pr(config, source_id, context.branch, title, summary, files, kind, phase)
201	    except GitServiceError:
202	        _return_to_branch(config.root_path, context.original_branch)
203	        raise
204	
205	    _record_change(config, files, sha, context.branch, pr_url, title, ingest_run_id, kind)
206	    _return_to_branch(config.root_path, context.original_branch)
207	    return CommitOutcome(
208	        branch=context.branch,
209	        commit_sha=sha,
210	        message=message,
211	        pr_url=pr_url,
212	        returned_to=context.original_branch,
213	    )

217	class _SourceGitState:
218	    id: int
219	    title: str | None
220	    git_branch: str | None
221	    git_pr_url: str | None

223	
224	def _load_source_git_state(config: WorkspaceConfig, source_id: int) -> "_SourceGitState | None":
225	    with open_session(config) as session:
226	        row = session.get(Source, source_id)
227	        if row is None:
228	            return None
229	        return _SourceGitState(
230	            id=row.id, title=row.title, git_branch=row.git_branch, git_pr_url=row.git_pr_url
231	        )

234	def _resume_source_branch(config: WorkspaceConfig, state: "_SourceGitState") -> str:
235	    root = config.root_path
236	    name = state.git_branch
237	    if git.branch_exists(root, name):
238	        try:
239	            git.checkout(root, name)
240	        except git.GitError as exc:
241	            raise GitServiceError(str(exc)) from exc
242	        return name
243	    if git.fetch_branch(root, name):
244	        try:
245	            git.checkout_new_tracking(root, name)
246	        except git.GitError as exc:
247	            raise GitServiceError(str(exc)) from exc
248	        return name
249	    # Branch is gone entirely -- most likely its PR was merged and GitHub
250	    # deleted it. Don't error: start a follow-up branch/PR for this source.
251	    return _create_fresh_branch(config, state.title or f"source-{state.id}", follow_up=True)
252

254	def _create_fresh_branch(config: WorkspaceConfig, title: str, follow_up: bool = False) -> str:
255	    root = config.root_path
256	    base = git.resolve_default_branch(root)
257	    branch_title = f"{title} revision" if follow_up else title
258	    name = ingest_branch_name(root, branch_title)
259	    try:
260	        git.create_branch_from(root, name, base)
261	    except git.GitError as exc:
262	        raise GitServiceError(str(exc)) from exc
263	    return name

266	def _remember_source_branch(config: WorkspaceConfig, source_id: int, branch: str) -> None:
267	    with open_session(config) as session:
268	        row = session.get(Source, source_id)
269	        if row is not None and not row.git_branch:
270	            row.git_branch = branch
271	        session.commit()

274	def _remember_source_pr(config: WorkspaceConfig, source_id: int, pr_url: str) -> None:
275	    with open_session(config) as session:
276	        row = session.get(Source, source_id)
277	        if row is not None:
278	            row.git_pr_url = pr_url
279	        session.commit()

282	def _return_to_branch(root, original_branch: str | None) -> None:
283	    if not original_branch:
284	        return
285	    # Best-effort; leave on the ingest branch rather than crash post-commit.
286	    with contextlib.suppress(git.GitError):
287	        git.checkout(root, original_branch)

290	def _phase_comment(phase: str, title: str, summary: str | None, files: list[str]) -> str:
291	    header = "Enrichment landed." if phase == "enrichment" else "Capture landed."
292	    lines = [header]
293	    if summary:
294	        lines += ["", summary]
295	    lines += ["", "Files:"]
296	    lines += [f"- `{path}`" for path in files]
297	    return "\n".join(lines)

300	def _land_pr(
301	    config: WorkspaceConfig,
302	    source_id: int,
303	    branch: str,
304	    title: str,
305	    summary: str | None,
306	    files: list[str],
307	    kind: str,
308	    phase: str,
309	) -> str | None:
310	    """Push the branch and create-or-update the source's PR. Returns None
311	    (not an error) when `gh` or a remote isn't available — branch/commit
312	    still happen either way; the PR is opportunistic."""
313	    if not gh_available():
314	        return None
315	    info = git.inspect_git(config.root_path)
316	    if not info.remote_url:
317	        return None
318	    try:
319	        git.push_branch(config.root_path, branch)
320	    except git.GitError as exc:
321	        raise GitServiceError(str(exc)) from exc
322	
323	    state = _load_source_git_state(config, source_id)
324	    existing_pr = state.git_pr_url if state else None
325	    if existing_pr:
326	        try:
327	            if phase == "enrichment":
328	                mark_pull_request_ready(config.root_path, existing_pr)
329	            comment_on_pull_request(
330	                config.root_path, existing_pr, _phase_comment(phase, title, summary, files)
331	            )
332	        except GhError as exc:
333	            raise GitServiceError(str(exc)) from exc
334	        return existing_pr
335	
336	    body_lines = [summary or f"Ingest of {title}.", "", "Files:"]
337	    body_lines += [f"- `{path}`" for path in files]
338	    body_lines += ["", "Review checklist:", "- [ ] Raw capture looks right"]
339	    body_lines += ["- [ ] Proposed note placement and links are correct"]
340	    draft = phase == "capture"
341	    try:
342	        pr_url = create_pull_request(
343	            config.root_path,
344	            commit_message(kind, f"add {title}"),
345	            "\n".join(body_lines),
346	            draft=draft,
347	        )
348	    except GhError as exc:
349	        raise GitServiceError(str(exc)) from exc
350	    _remember_source_pr(config, source_id, pr_url)
351	    return pr_url
352	
353	
354	def _record_change(
355	    config: WorkspaceConfig,
356	    files: list[str],
357	    sha: str,
358	    branch: str | None,
359	    pr_url: str | None,
360	    title: str,
361	    ingest_run_id: int | None,
362	    kind: str = "ingest",
363	) -> None:
364	    with open_session(config) as session:
365	        workspace_id = session.scalar(
366	            select(Workspace.id).where(Workspace.root_path == str(config.state_root))
367	        )
368	        session.add(
369	            GitChange(
370	                workspace_id=workspace_id,
371	                operation=f"{kind}-commit",
372	                branch_name=branch,
373	                commit_sha=sha,
374	                pr_url=pr_url,
375	                summary=f"{kind}: {title}",
376	                metadata_json=json.dumps({"files": files}),
377	            )
378	        )
379	        if ingest_run_id is not None:
380	            run = session.get(IngestRun, ingest_run_id)
381	            if run is not None:
382	                run.created_branch = branch
383	                run.created_commit = sha
384	                run.created_pr_url = pr_url
385	        session.commit()

54	| `ingest`  | 🧠    | enrichment output — raw capture turned into structured knowledge |

71	  the kind you'll reach for most often under this skill.

82	  entries). Until then, no wakil command produces this kind — use `note` or
83	  `ingest` for anything currently generated.
84

88	output exactly (`wakil <kind>: <description>`) as the base subject, adding

91	
92	## Procedure
93	
94	- [ ] Step 1: **Survey.** Run `wakil git summary` for branch, pending-change
95	      count, and recent commit context. For any single file whose history
96	      you need to understand before deciding where it belongs, `wakil git
97	      history <path>` shows its prior commits.
98

100	      status --porcelain` gives the file list; `git diff --stat` gives shape
101	      — neither is enough to decide grouping. Open the actual diff (`git
102	      diff <path>`, or read the first ~30 lines of an untracked file) for
103	      every changed path before deciding which change set it belongs to. Do
104	      not `git add -A` and commit as one blob — a note edit and an unrelated
105	      frontmatter fix picked up in the same sweep is exactly the failure
106	      mode this step prevents.
107	
108	- [ ] Step 3: **Group into logical change sets.** One coherent concern per
109	      commit: a single note's revision, one batch of related back-link
110	      additions, one schema-migrate type's mechanical fixes. Different notes
111	      touched for unrelated reasons are different commits even if they
112	      landed in the same session.
113	
114	- [ ] Step 4: **Exclude transient, generated, or sensitive files.** Don't
115	      stage SQLite WAL/journal files, caches, or anything that looks like
116	      local credentials — if something like that shows up modified, it's a
117	      sign it doesn't belong in this repo at all, not something to sweep
118	      into a commit. When in doubt, surface it and ask rather than silently
119	      staging or silently dropping it.
120	
121	- [ ] Step 5: **Confirm before committing.** State the proposed change sets
122	      (message + files) and get explicit approval before running `git
123	      commit` — this applies even to a single obviously-correct commit.
124	      Never commit destructive changes (a deletion, a large rewrite) without
125	      the user having seen the diff first. This mirrors wakil's own
126	      preview/confirm/apply discipline (`schema_migrate_service.py`'s
127	      propose → diff → confirm → apply split) — don't hold this skill to a
128	      lower bar than the code it's filling a gap around.
129	
130	- [ ] Step 6: **Write the message to describe the knowledge change, not the
131	      file list.** The subject line is `<emoji> wakil <kind>: <description>`
132	      in imperative, lowercase-first, no trailing period — the emoji is
133	      whichever one the commit convention table maps to `kind`, not a
134	      judgment call. The description names what changed about the knowledge
135	      base ("resynthesize Acme Corp state after Q3 update-call transcript",
136	      not "update acme-corp.md"). Add a body when the change isn't

138	      source it came from, what was added versus revised.
139	
140	- [ ] Step 7: **Commit each group, then re-verify.** After each commit, `git
141	      status --porcelain` again before staging the next group — confirm only
142	      the intended files moved and nothing unexpected is still sitting
143	      dirty.
144	
145	- [ ] Step 8: **Do not push** unless explicitly asked.

# wakil: Local Knowledge-Work Agent Plan

## Purpose

`wakil` is a local-first AI agent for working with a personal Markdown knowledge base.

The goal is not to build a broad agent platform, a coding assistant, or a complex multi-runtime system. The goal is to build a simple, pragmatic, powerful local assistant that helps a single user ingest, search, connect, revise, and reason over a Markdown knowledge base.

The target knowledge base is GBrain / Obsidian style: Markdown files, links, concepts, notes, project material, meeting transcripts, web clippings, and other personal knowledge artifacts.

The guiding product thesis is:

> Build a local, git-native knowledge-work agent that helps a single user discover useful connections, maintain a Markdown knowledge base, and turn raw inputs into durable, searchable memory.

The guiding engineering principle is:

> Keep the implementation simple unless added complexity has a clear and self-evident impact on the target use case.

Do not over-engineer this project.

17	### Unquoted `[[wikilink]]` in YAML frontmatter parses as a nested list
18	**Date:** 2026-07-18 · **Source:** session 0062da63-7923-40bd-b839-86cf8fb1d21f
19	
20	**Symptom:** An entity-revision smoke test kept failing with `validate_proposal` rejecting a `ref` field (e.g. `company`) as "expected a reference string, got list," even after the model's proposal was fixed — looking like a wakil merge/validation bug.
21	
22	**Root cause:** The test fixture's frontmatter had been hand-written with an unquoted wikilink, `company: [[companies/acme.md]]`. In YAML, unquoted `[[...]]` is flow-sequence syntax, not a wikilink string, so it parses as a nested list (`[['companies/acme.md']]`) before any wakil code sees it. Obsidian's `[[wikilink]]` convention only has meaning in Markdown body text — in raw YAML frontmatter it must be quoted (`company: "[[companies/acme.md]]"`), which is how real model-generated notes already format it.
23	
24	**Fix:** Quote wikilink-valued frontmatter fields as strings when hand-authoring fixtures or notes. If you see a `ref`-field validation error blaming a list value, check the source frontmatter for an unquoted `[[...]]` before suspecting the ingest/merge code.
25	
26	### FTS5 snippet() highlighting the wrong column
27	**Date:** 2026-07-17 · **Source:** `src/wakil/storage/fts.py` (commit 20b75a6)
28	
29	Search snippets in `search_notes`, `search_memories`, and `search_sources` could highlight the wrong part of a result. The `snippet()` calls hardcoded the column-index argument to `0`, which SQLite FTS5 takes literally as "always highlight the first column" — `title` in `notes_fts` (`["title", "path", "frontmatter_json"]`) and `sources_fts` (`["title", "origin", "author"]`) — rather than the column that actually matched the query. Since `0` is a valid column index, this ran without error and only surfaced as subtly wrong/misleading snippets. Fix: pass `-1`, FTS5's documented sentinel for "use the best-matching column," in all three `snippet()` calls.

### Commit-message emoji was a "manual commits only" presentation layer, so automatic commits silently lacked it
**Date:** 2026-07-23 · **Source:** `src/wakil/app/git_service.py`, `src/wakil/skills/kb-commit/SKILL.md`

**Symptom:** Commits made by `wakil ingest --commit`/`--branch`/`--pr` (on by default per ADR 0003) showed up in `git log` with no emoji (e.g. `wakil source: add mosaic offer sync ian gutwinski`), while the `kb-commit` skill's documented examples all showed an emoji-prefixed subject (`📥 wakil source: ...`) — read as a bug from the user's side.

**Root cause:** `commit_message()` deliberately returned the bare `wakil <kind>: <description>` string; `kb-commit/SKILL.md` described the emoji as a "presentation layer this skill adds on top of `commit_message()`'s output," applied only when a commit is hand-constructed by that skill, specifically to keep the function's own output unaffected. In practice all wakil-generated commits land in the same `git log`, so this was an inconsistency a user would see immediately, not an internal implementation seam — and no code anywhere actually parsed the bare format (confirmed by a full-codebase search before fixing), so the split had no real justification.

**Fix:** Moved the emoji into `commit_message()` itself (`COMMIT_EMOJI` dict, keyed by kind) so every wakil-generated commit — automatic CLI flag or `kb-commit`'s manual commit — carries the same prefix. When a "presentation layer added on top of a shared helper" is actually visible to the end user (not just internal/programmatic consumers), prefer folding it into the helper rather than splitting it across two call paths that both write to the same user-visible log.
